column3: KAZAN-YU — SUMMIT PLAN (+120 m): top-down plan of the crater rim. The spring source with hanging egg baskets steaming at D2, the Caldera Crown Infinity Pool with its infinity edge spilling south over the rim toward the clouds, the Tsukimi moon-viewing deck pavilion at H2 with the head of the Cliff Stair, the cable lift top station at E4, and the head of the Terrace Path and Cascade Terraces starting down the south-west slope. Rocky crater, steam vents, lanterns along rim walkways.

KAZAN-YU — GROUND LEVEL PLAN (0 m): top-down plan. The approach road arrives from the west to the black basalt torii Basalt Gate at A4; the arrival hall C3–E4 with its long glass lava window wall, slipper cubbies and stone basin; the main lift and Spiral Stair at E3; changing halls F3–G4 with lockers and showers; the cable lift base at E4; the foot of the Terrace Path and the lowest Cascade Terrace pools outdoors at B5; the start of the Cliff Stair at G3 heading to the north cliff suites. The outer mountain slope shown around the edges.

KAZAN-YU — NORTH CLIFF SUITES: a presentation sheet with TWO drawings side by side. LEFT: front elevation of the north cliff face showing about 12 suites stacked in 4 tiers carved into the basalt, each with a glowing window, a ledge with a private stone onsen tub, a small waterfall trickle feeding each tub from the one above, and the zig-zag Cliff Stair connecting Ground to every suite landing and up to the moon deck at the top. RIGHT: a top-down plan of one typical suite: entry, tatami room, futon, washi screens, the tub ledge, the trickle channel. Same rendered plan style.

KAZAN-YU — LEVEL B1 THERMAL PLAN (−20 m): top-down plan. A network of misty ankle-deep reflecting-pool corridors with stepping stones links: the Fumarole Steam Grotto at C2–D3 (a chain of three steam rooms labeled 45 °C, 55 °C, 65 °C with basalt benches and wooden buckets), the Obsidian Mirror Float Pool at E2–F3 (a perfectly black round pool under a glowworm dome), treatment rooms at G3–H4 (massage rooms with stone tables), the Glacier Plunge Ice Cave at I2–J3 (blue ice, cold pool, a door straight back to the steam), the Magma Glass Slide launch platform and the head of the Lava Stair at H4 next to a lava glow, the main lift and Spiral Stair at E3, and the Mist Steps descending to B2 at C3. Lanterns, koi ponds at corridor junctions.

KAZAN-YU — LEVEL B2 RIVER PLAN (−40 m): top-down plan. The glowing turquoise underground river enters at the east edge J2 and flows WEST across the level to a rock lip at B3 where it drops away (labeled "TO THUNDER CURTAIN FALLS"). Over the river at C2–F3 the KAWAGIRI restaurant: timber decks on beams, 12 private table pods each boxed by a "WATER CURTAIN", fine hinoki aqueduct lines (soy and tea) branching to every table, the kitchen with its steam vent, magenta and cyan neon. The neon RAMEN COUNTER at F3. The BOAT LANDING at G3 with lantern boats. A riverside boardwalk along the whole river. The Mist Steps arriving from B1 at C3, the main lift and Spiral Stair at E3, the Falls Stair heading down at B3–B4.

KAZAN-YU — LEVEL B3 AQUA CAVERN PLAN (−70 m): top-down plan of one huge cavern. At B3 the 9 THUNDER CURTAIN FALLS plunge pool with the Falls Stair and the walkway behind the falls; 8 RIMSTONE CASCADE TERRACES at C3–D5 as dozens of scalloped stepped pools; 2 LAVA TUBE LAZY RIVER as a loop tunnel (shown with a dashed roof outline) around D4–G5 with float rings; 4 GEYSER PLAZA at F4 as a circular plaza with a ring of stone seats and geyser vents; the 3 MAGMA GLASS SLIDE splashdown pool and the foot of the Lava Stair at H4 beside a lava glow; 10 WAVE GROTTO at I4–J5 as a black sand beach with waves and the sea mouth opening on the east edge. A shore path connects everything. The main lift and Spiral Stair at E3. Numbered attraction legend.

KAZAN-YU — LEVEL B4 MAGMA CHAMBER PLAN (−100 m): top-down plan of the deepest level. The lift lobby and foot of the Spiral Stair at E3; a curving tunnel gallery leading to the long sealed MAGMA VIEWING CHAMBER at C5–F6, with a continuous wall of thick glass and molten lava beyond it glowing orange, benches, a hush zone. Small and atmospheric, mostly dark rock.

KAZAN-YU — LEVEL ALIGNMENT KEY: a precise technical coordination drawing for 3D modelling. LEFT two thirds: one shared A–J / 1–6 grid with the outlines of all seven levels overlaid in different line colours (Summit, Ground, B1, B2, B3, B4, plus the north cliff suites), each with a few key labels, and the vertical connections drawn as bold symbols at fixed cells: main lift and Spiral Stair at E3, Mist Steps at C3, Falls Stair at B3–B4, Lava Stair and slide at H4, cable lift at E4, Cliff Stair along G3–H2, Terrace Path along B5–E3. RIGHT third: a vertical elevation strip listing levels with elevations (+120, 0, −20, −40, −70, −100) and which stairs and lifts connect each pair of levels, and a legend. Clean, technical, still on the dark charcoal style.
